stops.name: Slindon, Sussex, The Quest of the Spirit
stops.campa: By 1913 the Astleys are settled at Slindon in Sussex, and there is published in London The Quest of the Spirit: by a Pilgrim of the Way, Astley's book, which she edits and owns as her own. 'In editing the work,' she writes, 'I feel that it is the expression of my own thought and aspiration, though voiced by another.' The teacher of the outward body has become the seeker of the inward light; the two lives, public and hidden, are made one in this single volume of the mystic quest.
stops.quote: In editing the work, I feel that it is the expression of my own thought and aspiration, though voiced by another.
stops.quote_source: Genevieve Stebbins, editor's note to The Quest of the Spirit (1913)

stops.name: Monterey, the return to the native shore
stops.campa: Before the Great War is out, the Astleys give up their lifelong lease in Sussex and return across the ocean to California: to Monterey, on the Pacific shore of the state where sixty years before she was born. By 1920 they are living on Del Monte Avenue. The great circle is closing: the actress who crossed the whole continent to the New York stage has come home to the far western sea. The public life is long behind her; only the hidden work remains, and the closing of the ring.

stops.name: Carmel-by-the-Sea, the mentors of the Brotherhood of Light
stops.campa: At Carmel-by-the-Sea the Astleys become mentors to the young Elbert Benjamine, and it is they who help draw him to Los Angeles to found the Brotherhood of Light in 1918. Through Astley, through Burgoyne, through Zanoni, the old hermetic current of the Brotherhood of Luxor passes on into the new order, and Stebbins's hidden decades feed its lessons. The teacher of the American body has become, at the last, a mother of an American esoteric church, her influence flowing on unseen as it once flowed into the dance.

stops.name: Monterey, the last certain record
stops.campa: On 21 September 1934, at Monterey, Geneviève Stebbins Astley dies, aged seventy-seven. Her death falls in the very year Elbert Benjamine completes the Brotherhood of Light lessons, the hidden work sealed as her outward life ends. Within a week Astley marries the nurse who tended her, and departs for England. She leaves behind the manuals that are her canon and a lineage she never claimed: the breath and the attitudes she taught, carried by her pupils' pupils, standing at the root of modern dance: the American station between Delsarte and Laban.
